title: Idempotent projection for a pair henselization fibre
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal and c a colimit cocone of the full category of etale maps A to D inducing bijections A/I to D/ID. Write B=c.pt.right, f:A to B, and suppose B is Noetherian. Let C be a commutative ring, g:B to C, q a prime of B, p its contraction, and rho:kappa(p) to kappa(q) the canonical A-algebra residue map. Give C the B-algebra structure from g and A-algebra structure from g composed with f. If phi:p.Fiber C to q.Fiber C is a ring homomorphism satisfying phi(x tensor y)=rho(x) tensor y on every pure tensor, then there is e in p.Fiber C such that e is idempotent, phi(e)=1, phi is surjective, and every x in ker(phi) satisfies e*x=0.

proof.text: Use filteredness of the pair-etale category and its essential smallness. Transport the under-category colimit along commAlgCatEquivUnder and reindex along equivSmallModel in the universe of A. Apply the finite-separable-fibres theorem to the resulting small diagram, and transport its canonical decomposition to B=c.pt.right. This yields the finite product of all residue fields over p and separable algebraicity of each extension.

The canonical decomposition respects the B-algebra structures: on each component, x tensor b maps to rho(x) times the residue image of b, so 1 tensor b maps to the structure-map image of b. Tensor this B-algebra equivalence over B with C. Tensor cancellation identifies the source with kappa(p) tensor_A C, while distribution over the finite product identifies the target with the product of kappa(q_i) tensor_B C. The component at q sends x tensor y to rho(x) tensor y. The hypothesis on phi identifies phi with this projection because pure tensors additively generate the source.

In the product of fibres choose e equal to 1 at q and 0 elsewhere and pull it back to p.Fiber C. Componentwise multiplication gives idempotence and phi(e)=1. Extension by zero gives surjectivity of phi. For x in its kernel the q coordinate is zero, while all other coordinates of e are zero, so e*x=0. This also applies to zero components.

lean.statement:
theorem pair_henselization_fiber_projection
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦
        AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map D.hom) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map D.hom.hom) D.hom.hom
            (Ideal.le_comap_map)))))
    (hc : IsColimit c) [IsNoetherianRing c.pt.right]
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] (g : c.pt.right →+* C)
    (q : Ideal c.pt.right) [q.IsPrime] :
    letI := c.pt.hom.hom.toAlgebra
    letI := g.toAlgebra
    letI := (g.comp c.pt.hom.hom).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A c.pt.right C :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
    let p := q.comap c.pt.hom.hom
    ∀ (ρ : p.ResidueField →ₐ[A] q.ResidueField),
      ρ = Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p q (Algebra.ofId A c.pt.right) rfl →
    ∀ (φ : p.Fiber C →+* q.Fiber C),
      (∀ (x : p.ResidueField) (y : C),
        φ (TensorProduct.tmul A x y) = TensorProduct.tmul c.pt.right (ρ x) y) →
      ∃ e : p.Fiber C, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ φ e = 1 ∧
        Function.Surjective φ ∧ ∀ x, φ x = 0 → e * x = 0
